creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Every Claude Code pane in the devenv window came back blank after a relaunch on 2026-09-09: an empty pane with the cursor in the bottom-left corner, the process alive, and herdr's own grid for the pane empty. The two bash panes in the same tab rendered normally. Measured on 0.7.0 / herdr 0.8.0 / Claude Code 2.1.266, window 55746 quitting at 13:10:28 and window 87686 launching at 13:10:46 (times local, UTC-5).

## What the quit did

`quitting()` in `crates/muster-seam/src/session.rs` hands every attached pane back at the size herdr's own layout gives it (`quit.geometry.restored asked=9 settled=9`), so that a herdr TUI opened later does not inherit Muster's geometry (`a_29ryxUDCY`). With no real client, herdr's layout for this nine-pane workspace reads as an 80x24 screen split nine ways. From `/home/.config/herdr/sessions/muster/herdr-server.log`, one second before the clients detached:

    18:10:27Z client resize client_id=107 cols=26 rows=10   w6:pG, a Claude that was 173x39
    18:10:27Z client resize client_id=108 cols=26 rows=12   w6:pD, a Claude that was 173x47
    18:10:27Z client resize client_id=109 cols=26 rows=6    w6:pK, a Claude that was 173x23
    18:10:27Z client resize client_id=106 cols=26 rows=3    w6:p5, a bash shell that was 173x13
    18:10:28Z client detached (all nine)

Claude Code redraws the whole screen on a width change, starting with `\e[2J\e[H` (measured twice below). So every agent's screen was redrawn for 26 columns, and herdr held no scrollback for those panes afterwards (`herdr pane list`: `max_offset_from_bottom: 0`).

## What came back

The relaunch attached at the real sizes (`client connected client_id=116 cols=173 rows=39`; `stty size` on the box confirmed every PTY back at 173 columns) and each bridge got a first frame. The four Claude panes stayed blank for thirteen minutes:

- `muster pane read` with no `--rows` returned zero rows, `herdr pane read w6:pG --source visible` returned nothing, and `herdr pane list` reported no scrollback. The grid was empty; this was not a rendering fault.
- The processes were healthy: `Sl+`, sleeping in `ep_poll`, in the foreground process group of their PTY.
- A rows-only resize (`stty -F /dev/pts/5 rows 38`, then `39`) made that Claude write `\e[?2026h\e[?25l\e[38;3H\e[?25h\e[?2026l` and nothing else: a cursor move to its input row. It believed its UI was on screen.
- The window resized every pane 173 to 79 to 173 columns at 13:16:26, a width change, and the grids were still empty at 13:20.
- At 13:23:48 all five Claude bridges received frames in the same instant (`bridge.frames` for pG, p1, pD, pK and pA) and the panes were back. Another agent was editing `/home/.claude/settings.json` on the box at the time (final mtime 13:25:33). Claude Code re-renders when its settings file changes, which fits five simultaneous repaints; inferred from timing, not observed.

Not reproduced in isolation. A fresh Claude in tmux on the box, on the chat screen, resized 173x39 to 26x10 to 173x39, redrew in full on the grow (`\e[2J\e[H` and the whole screen). The tiny size alone does not blank a Claude. Candidates for the missing ingredient: a long transcript, the 24 seconds spent at 26 columns with no client attached, or herdr's grid across a detach and reattach.

The run log could not say whether the 13:16:27 redraw landed: `bridge.frames` is written only when a frame arrives at least a second after the previous summary, so one redraw after a quiet spell never appears.

## What it costs

- Every quit, `brew upgrade` included, redraws every agent on every daemon for 26 columns, and the transcript that was on screen is gone when the window comes back.
- Here it also left four agents blank for thirteen minutes while the sidebar showed their states, every bridge was healthy, and the run log carried no warning or error.
- The handoff serves a herdr TUI nobody opens on these sessions. Muster is the only client, and it sets its own size on attach.

## Directions

- Stop shrinking on quit. Leave each pane at the size it has; the next Muster resizes it on attach, and a herdr TUI would inherit a real terminal size rather than 26x3. `a_29ryxUDCY` records why the handoff exists; the cost measured here is larger than the one it prevents.
- A pane whose first frame is empty while herdr says it holds an idle agent could be reported, since "blank pane, healthy bridge, idle agent" is what this looked like from inside the window.

## Validating a fix

- Quit a window with a Claude in a pane, relaunch. `herdr-server.log` shows no `client resize` before the detach, the transcript is still on screen, and `muster pane read` on the pane returns it.
title: 🫙 A quit shrinks every pane to herdr's own layout, and every Claude came back blank
